historical_record.description: Bliss & Faville designed the Bank of Italy building.
Hallidie Plaza branch of the Bank of Italy. Designed by Bliss & Faville.

About 300 demonstrators sang freedom songs outside the Bank of America branch here in 1964, facing a hostile crowd of 800 to 1,000 across the street, in the statewide campaign that led banks to sign oversight agreements with the Fair Employment Practices Commission.
The buildings that had hidden the bank from Market Street were demolished to make Hallidie Plaza.
An existing seven-story over basement building stood on the site, with a ground-level banking institution and office uses above.
The building, originally the Bank of Italy, was constructed in 1920.
The City Planning Commission approved Section 309 determination of compliance for minor ground-floor entrance and window modifications and seismic retrofit of the seven-story building, 7-0.

The City Planning Commission approved the Section 309 determination of compliance for conversion of the office portion of the existing building to approximately 44 residential units within the existing envelope.
